long_biography.plain_text:
Growing up in Newark, Dennis Kozlowski worked multiple jobs before earning a business degree from Seton Hall and joining Tyco International early in his career. He rose through operating and finance roles to become chief executive, then built the company through scores of acquisitions. Tyco evolved into a global conglomerate spanning fire and security systems, medical products, electronics, flow control and telecommunications, with Kozlowski known for tight cost control and rapid integration.

That ascent ended after his 2002 resignation and prosecution. A New York jury convicted him of grand larceny, falsifying business records, conspiracy and securities fraud; the state's highest court later upheld the convictions. After more than eight years in prison, he was released on parole in 2014. Kozlowski now runs an M&A and business-consulting practice and chairs the Fortune Society, a nonprofit supporting people returning from incarceration.
